newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. senator in Syria for Israel -- official source.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator in Syria for Israel -- official source.

text.p: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter was holding talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus at the request of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, an Israeli government official said on Wednesday.
The official, who spoke on condition that he not be named, confirmed to Reuters an Israel Radio report that Specter was on a "mission" for Netanyahu.

"This morning there was a meeting between Specter and Netanyahu and (U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin) Indyk and tomorrow there will be another meeting when he returns from Damascus, from Assad, obviously," the official said.
He said Specter left Israel for Damascus immediately after meeting Netanyahu in the morning.
Syrian presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said on Wednesday that Assad held talks with Specter in Damascus.
Kourieh said Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara and U.S. ambassador to Syria Christopher Ross were present at the meeting at the presidential palace.
The United States, sponsor of Arab-Israeli peace talks, has played the role of a mediator to defuse tension between Syria and Israel that has shot up since Netanyahu took office in June.
The two arch foes have held sporadic peace talks for the last five years. The negotiations have long snagged over the Golan Heights which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Syria demands a full Israeli withdrawal from the Golan Heights. Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May elections, had publicly said it could make at least a partial withdrawal for full peace.
Netanyahu opposes the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace. Negotiations between the sides have yet to resume under Netanyahu.
